title: How to Break Up With Your Phone

questions.q: Why are phones so addictive, according to the summary?
a: Each small interaction releases dopamine
They provide unlimited access to news
They connect you with family all day
They are designed to improve memory
questions.why: Lesson one says dopamine rewards each check, prompting the brain to repeat the behavior again and again.

questions.q: What does the summary say constant phone use does to the mind?
a: It weakens attention and short-term memory
It improves multitasking and reaction speed
It makes learning new skills easier
It has no measurable effect on thinking
questions.why: Lesson two says phones affect short-term memory and attention span because a glance away makes you forget your task.

questions.q: Why is the brain so quick to choose distraction over focus?
a: Spotting distractions once helped humans survive
Distraction uses more energy than focus
Phones train the brain to ignore danger
Focus is a skill only children have
questions.why: Lesson two explains that watchfulness helped our ancestors spot threats, and focus costs the brain more energy.

questions.q: What is the first step to changing your relationship with your phone?
a: Notice which activities pull you to it and why
Delete every social media account at once
Buy a phone with fewer features
Set a strict one-hour daily limit
questions.why: Lesson three says awareness of what you are doing on the phone must come before deciding which habits to change.

questions.q: What must the decision to use your phone less come from?
a: A genuine personal desire to change
A friend's insistence that you stop
A new app that tracks your usage
A doctor's warning about screen time
questions.why: The summary says the change should not come from reading a book, but from really wanting to fix the behavior.
